# The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27

First listed: 2025-09-29 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PT6payqqvuk) - 2025-09-29
- [Substack: The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-ai-revolution-winners-losers-41b) - 2025-09-29

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Dan Ives offers a broad AI bull case spanning identity, infrastructure, Apple distribution, Tesla autonomy, Palantir and small nuclear reactors. Eisman repeatedly probes adoption, operating proof, timing, interim earnings and China risk. Most precise operating visions extend to 2027-2032 and remain open; the xAI investment direction happened later than the specified November 2025 date. Important guest premises on European zero adoption and Palantir having no sales force are contradicted by primary evidence.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Separate revolutionary technology from winners and losers.
- Ask whether an incumbent moat protects renewals or merely historical profits.
- Differentiate earnings forecasts from stock-price forecasts.
- Demand operating and regulatory milestones for pre-revenue technology.
- Identify how network utility actually accrues to token holders.
- Trace second-order beneficiaries while checking their distinct economics.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- AI capex and aggregate cash comparison
- Tesla earnings versus share price
- Apple $270-$280 target
- Palantir three-to-five-year trillion-dollar scenario
- Oklo deployment milestones
- World verification adoption target

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Dan Ives. Most specific technology and price forecasts are Ives; Eisman often questions rather than endorses them.
- Opening montage duplicates later claims.
- Publication is September 29, but discussion of the September 8 Eightco announcement as this week implies earlier recording; exact recording date not established.
- Captions garble Eightco, Oklo, Palantir and decimal stock prices.
- Perplexity/Google references appear confused; do not infer a verified ownership relationship.
- Ives discloses chairmanship/ETF interests; promotional exposure is relevant context.
- Guest forecasts are not Eisman forecasts.
